memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the day the tabernacle, the tent of the covenant law, was set up, the cloud covered it. From evening till morning the cloud above the tabernacle looked like fire. That is how it continued to be; the cloud covered it, and at night it looked like fire. - Num 9:15-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gave His people a visible sign of His presence: a cloud over the tabernacle by day, and by night the cloud looked like fire. Wherever they camped, this sign hovered over God's dwelling place. Day and night, they could look up and see it — a constant reminder that God was truly with them.

Imagine the comfort of this. In a vast, empty wilderness, surrounded by uncertainty, God's people could see with their own eyes that He had not left them. He was there, over the tabernacle, morning and night. His presence was not a distant hope; it was visible and near.

We do not have a cloud and fire over our homes today. But the truth those signs pointed to is more true for us than ever: God is with His people. Through Christ, God's presence has come to dwell not just among us but within us by His Spirit (1 Cor 3:16).

The cloud by day and fire by night also remind us that God is with us in every season — in the brightness of day and the darkness of night. When life is dark and uncertain, His presence appears as a comforting fire; when the way is clear, His presence overshadows us like a sheltering cloud.

You may not see a visible sign, but you can be just as sure: God is with you. Jesus promised, "I am with you always" (Matt 28:20). Look up in faith and know that your God has not left you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you live aware that God is truly present with you?
- How does God's presence comfort you in dark and uncertain times?
- What helps you remember He is with you when you cannot "see" Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You are truly present with Your people, by day and by night. Help me to live today certain that You are with me, in Christ. Amen.
